items.locator: AACN — Nurse Residency Program: the Vizient/AACN Nurse Residency Program is an evidence-based transition-to-practice program for new entry-level nurses, supporting professional development, application of competencies, quality/safety, leadership, and transition into the practice environment.
items.version: Current AACN nurse-residency program guidance live-rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.version: Current ANCC Magnet Recognition Program guidance live-rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.source_name: The Joint Commission — Credentialing and Privileging: Licensed Practitioners
items.locator: The Joint Commission credentialing/privileging FAQ, updated 2026-01-07: applicable APRNs/PAs and other licensed practitioners providing medical-level care must be credentialed and granted appropriate clinical privileges before providing those services; qualifications, requested services, law/regulation, education/training, licensure and current competence are considered through the organization's process.
items.version: Joint Commission FAQ last updated 2026-01-07; current standards interpretation live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: A hospital is onboarding an APRN who will write orders, perform histories and physicals, and direct medical-level care within state law. Which organizational action is required before the APRN provides these services?

options.A: Allow the APRN to begin once payroll onboarding is complete because professional licensure automatically grants all hospital clinical privileges.
options.B: Limit the review to employment references because state licensure replaces the hospital's credentialing and privileging process for medical-level care.
options.C: Credential the APRN and grant appropriate clinical privileges through the organization's process, consistent with law, qualifications, and requested services, before care begins.
options.D: Permit unrestricted provisional practice first and complete credentialing and privileging only after the APRN has already performed the requested services.

items.rationale: Joint Commission guidance requires applicable licensed practitioners, including APRNs providing medical-level care, to be credentialed and granted appropriate clinical privileges before those services are provided. Option C correctly links the organization's process to law, qualifications, competence, and the requested scope. Options A and B incorrectly treat licensure or employment review as substitutes. Option D reverses the required sequence by allowing services before privileges are granted.

items.source_name: 2026 AHA/ACC Multisociety Guideline for Acute Pulmonary Embolism
items.locator: 2026 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ACEP/CHEST/SCAI/SHM/SIR/SVM/SVN Guideline for Evaluation and Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism — Section 3.1.1 Clinical Assessment/Pretest Probability: validated clinical pretest-probability tools include the Wells score and Revised Geneva score and are used before definitive testing to guide the diagnostic pathway.
items.version: Multisociety acute PE guideline published 2026-02-19 and current in 2026; live guideline source rechecked 2026-08-15. Blueprint corrected to Reduction of Risk Potential because the item tests diagnostic probability assessment rather than acute physiologic management.
items.stem: A client presents with symptoms concerning for pulmonary embolism. The clinician calculates a Wells score before deciding on D-dimer testing or imaging. What does the Wells score estimate?

options.A: The short-term mortality risk after pulmonary embolism has already been confirmed by imaging.
options.B: The probability of major bleeding after therapeutic anticoagulation has been started.
options.C: The severity of right-ventricular dysfunction once pulmonary embolism is diagnosed.
options.D: The clinical pretest probability that pulmonary embolism is present before definitive imaging.

items.rationale: The 2026 multisociety pulmonary-embolism guideline uses validated pretest-probability tools such as the Wells score to estimate how likely PE is before definitive testing and to guide the diagnostic pathway. Option D states that purpose. Options A, B, and C describe prognosis, bleeding risk, or severity assessment after diagnosis rather than pretest probability. The blueprint is therefore Reduction of Risk Potential, not Physiological Adaptation.

items.locator: StatPearls Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm — clinical presentation/rupture: rupture can present with sudden severe abdominal and/or back/flank pain, hypotension/shock, tachycardia, and sometimes a pulsatile abdominal mass; suspected rupture is a vascular emergency requiring immediate evaluation and management.
items.version: StatPearls [Internet], current 2026 NCBI Bookshelf entry; clinical content live-rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: StatPearls Pericarditis — History and Physical/acute pericarditis: chest pain is classically sharp and pleuritic, worse supine and improved sitting up or leaning forward; a pericardial friction rub is a characteristic and highly specific finding when present.
items.version: Current 2026 StatPearls Pericarditis entry in NCBI Bookshelf; live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
